A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DynamiCS study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite table relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original VLM training experiments, classification and retrieval evaluations, robustness results, and ablations in Sections 5–6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds cluster-refinement threshold results and expanded computational-cost accounting.

M1.justification: Cluster scaling, epoch-wise sampling, centroid merging, and model architectures remain unchanged. The replacement-sampling statement and greedy-merging description clarify existing components; they do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Training datasets and classification, retrieval, long-tail, and robustness coverage are retained. Table 9's caption changes from 25 to 22 datasets, but both versions contain the same 22 dataset columns.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in corresponding experiments is unchanged, including DFN and reproduced DFN*, RECLIP, CLIPA, HQ-CLIP, and full-training baselines. Corrected citations do not introduce replacement methods. SuperKMeans is discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: New Table 17 evaluates seven fusion thresholds from 0.6 to 1.0 using DataComp, 106 million samples seen, ViT-B/16, and 112×112 images. Table 15 adds end-to-end GPU-hour totals and preprocessing/training overhead ratios. Existing experimental settings, including the default 0.7 threshold, are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix D.1 adds a sensitivity study testing how centroid-fusion thresholds affect ImageNet accuracy and retained centroid counts. Appendix C additionally analyzes preprocessing overhead across training budgets. Earlier sampling, scaling-factor, cluster-count, batch-size, and robustness analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed counts, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. The added results retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark-table scores are unchanged. New Table 17 reports, for example, 39.2% accuracy with 10,808 retained centroids at threshold 0.7 versus 34.9% with 50,000 at 1.0. New Table 15 gives totals of 119.25, 187.25, and 323.25 GPU-hours. Several prose summaries are corrected against unchanged tables: Section 6.2 now reports a 0.5-point margin over DFN* instead of 2.6 over DFN, and Section 6.5 corrects long-tail margins against OpenAI-WIT/OpenCLIP from 7.7/6.4 to 14.1/12.9 points.

T1.justification: Equations 1–2, scaling-factor cases, and assumptions about semantic embeddings are retained. Explaining the existing symbol N and correcting the cluster index clarify notation; no new theoretical result, derivation, or proof appears.

C1.justification: Both versions claim efficient, long-tail-aware training through cluster scaling and dynamic sampling, with competitive full-training performance at approximately 3% of training cost. v2 foregrounds cluster scaling and restates the existing diversity and upsampling rationale without changing the claims' substantive scope.

C2.justification: Appendix C extends the existing offline-cost discussion by explaining how combined embedding/clustering overhead becomes proportionally smaller as training scales and discussing potentially faster clustering. Earlier interpretations of long-tail benefits, retrieval shortcomings, and unusual frequency-performance cases are retained.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents sampling with replacement when the target cluster size exceeds its original size, details the greedy cosine-similarity merging rule, and reports a 0.25 GPU-hour merging cost. The code URL moves from an introduction footnote to the abstract; this does not establish newly available code.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Reproducible Scaling Laws for Contrastive Language-Image Learning paper and SuperKMeans, while retaining the OpenCLIP software reference. Research positioning otherwise remains stable; most reference edits concern numbering, capitalization, metadata, or attribution corrections.

P1.justification: v2 corrects grammar, terminology, cross-references, and author affiliation/contact information. It reorders contribution bullets and explanatory paragraphs to discuss cluster scaling before dynamic sampling, while preserving the overall section structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds the cost-breakdown and fusion-threshold tables, relocates several existing tables, and revises captions. v1 Tables 15–17 correspond to v2 Tables 16, 18, and 19. Figures 1–3 retain their visual content; there is no broad graphical redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reporting accuracy by correcting numerical summaries to match existing tables, makes implementation details clearer, and supplies evidence for the existing refinement threshold. The expanded cost breakdown makes preprocessing overhead easier to assess. These are useful, limited gains in correctness, reproducibility, and transparency; the central method and benchmark evidence remain unchanged.
